The memo accurately reflects the key financial terms present in the source document. The main financial term mentioned - the US$750,000,000 threshold for "Qualifying Material Acquisition" - is directly supported by Section 2 of the source document. The memo appropriately notes "N/A" for terms not provided in this amendment document (such as interest rates, maturity dates, loan amounts, etc.), which is accurate since this is only an amendment focused on modifying the acquisition definition rather than a comprehensive credit agreement. All borrower/lender names, dates, and other material terms mentioned in the memo are consistent with the source document.

MISSING_TERMS: None

The memo appropriately captures all the key financial terms that are actually present in this amendment document. This is specifically a limited amendment that only modifies the definition of "Qualifying Material Acquisition" and sets the threshold at US$750,000,000. The memo correctly notes that this document doesn't contain the broader deal terms (interest rates, maturity dates, loan amounts, etc.) since those would be in the original 2020 credit agreement. The memo appropriately identifies the key parties (Otis Worldwide Corporation as borrower, JPMorgan Chase as Administrative Agent), the amendment date (April 20, 2022), and the material financial threshold being modified ($750MM acquisition threshold including all associated costs and assumed debt). All substantive financial terms present in the source document are reflected in the memo.
